The '''2017–18 Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball team''' represented [[Florida Gulf Coast University]] in the [[2017–18 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Eagles were led by fifth-year head coach [[Joe Dooley (basketball)|Joe Dooley]] and played their home games at [[Alico Arena]] in [[Fort Myers, Florida]] as members of the [[Atlantic Sun Conference]]. They finished the season 23–12, 12–2 in ASUN play to win the ASUN regular season championship. In the [[2018 Atlantic Sun men's basketball tournament|ASUN tournament]], they defeated [[2017–18 USC Upstate Spartans men's basketball team|USC Upstate]] and [[2017–18 North Florida Ospreys men's basketball team|North Florida]] to advance to the championship game where they lost to [[2017–18 Lipscomb Bisons men's basketball team|Lipscomb]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2018/03/01/lipscomb-basketball-earns-berth-atlantic-sun-championship-after-crushing-jacksonville/387082002/|title=Lipscomb basketball earns berth in Atlantic Sun championship after crushing Jacksonville|work=The Tennessean|access-date=2018-05-16|language=en}}</ref> As a regular season conference champion who failed to win their conference tournament, they received an automatic bid to the [[2018 National Invitation Tournament|National Invitation Tournament]] where they lost in the first round to [[2017–18 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team|Oklahoma State]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2018/03/13/oklahoma-state-tops-fgcu-80-68-in-nit-opening-round/32912775/|title=Oklahoma State tops FGCU 80-68 in NIT opening round|work=USA TODAY|access-date=2018-05-16|language=en}}</ref>

On April 4, 2018, head coach Joe Dooley left the school to become the head coach at [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina]], where he was previously the head coach from 1995 to 1999.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/article207973694.html|title=East Carolina brings back Dooley as its men's hoops coach|work=kentucky|access-date=2018-04-05|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040519/http://www.kentucky.com/sports/article207973694.html|archive-date=2018-04-06|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/23032046/east-carolina-pirates-bring-back-joe-dooley-men-basketball-coach|title=Dooley returns to ECU for 2nd coaching stint|work=ESPN.com|access-date=2018-05-16}}</ref> The following day, assistant head coach [[Michael Fly]] was promoted to head coach.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.naplesnews.com/story/sports/college/fgcu/2018/04/05/fgcu-name-longtime-assistant-michael-fly-new-mens-basketball-head-coach/488617002/|title=FGCU names longtime assistant Michael Fly as new men's basketball head coach|newspaper=[[Naples Daily News]]|first=Dana|last=Caldwell|date=April 5, 2018|accessdate=April 6, 2018}}</ref>

== Previous season ==
The [[2016–17 Florida Gulf Coast Eagles men's basketball team|Eagles]] finished the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]] 26–8, 12–2 in [[2016–17 Atlantic Sun Conference men's basketball season|ASUN play]] to win the regular season championship.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://scout.com/college/florida-gulf-coast/Article/Zach-Johnson-shoots-FGCU-to-win-over-Stetson-74923427|title=Zach Johnson shoots FGCU to win over Stetson|work=FGCUEaglesNest.com|access-date=2017-07-27}}</ref> As the No. 1 seed in the [[2017 Atlantic Sun men's basketball tournament|ASUN tournament]], they defeated [[2016–17 Stetson Hatters men's basketball team|Stetson]], [[2016–17 Kennesaw State Owls men's basketball team|Kennesaw State]], and [[2016–17 North Florida Ospreys men's basketball team|North Florida]] to win the tournament championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400945332|title=North Florida vs. Florida Gulf Coast - Game Recap - March 5, 2017 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2017-07-27}}</ref> As a result, they received the conference's automatic bid to the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. As a No. 14 seed in the West region, they lost in the first round to No. 3-seeded [[2016–17 Florida State Seminoles men's basketball team|Florida State]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.oregonlive.com/march-madness/index.ssf/2017/03/florida_state_vs_fgcu_ncaa_tournament.html|title=Florida State defeats Florida Gulf Coast: NCAA Tournament first round|work=OregonLive.com|access-date=2017-07-27|language=en-US}}</ref>
